title: Scratch test results grid
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Making materials (9E); conservation of energy
source: Seeded from science/y9 lesson 17 (Scratch test results grid (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 17: Testing hardness safely at home. To understand how a scratch test compares the hardness of materials

questions.q: The steel key scratches a tile but the coin does not. Estimate the tile's hardness.
questions.model: The coin (3.5) cannot scratch it, so it is harder than 3.5. The key (5.5) can, so it is softer than 5.5. So between 3.5 and 5.5.

questions.q: Why test with the softest tester first?
questions.a: So we find the lowest tester that scratches, without damaging the sample more than needed.

questions.q: What does a streak that wipes off show?
questions.a: The tester left material behind; it is not a scratch.

questions.q: Core: Scratch-test five household materials with a fingernail, a coin and a steel key. Record and rank them.
questions.a: Pupils' own, e.g. soap and candle softest, plastic, then tile hardest.
questions.model: Teacher tests soap on camera: fingernail scratches it, so it is below 2.5.

questions.q: Extend: Explain why the unglazed back of a tile is harder to scratch than plastic.
questions.a: Ceramic particles are held by strong bonds in a rigid structure; plastic chains can be pushed apart.

questions.q: Stretch: Evaluate your test: how could you make it more reliable?
questions.a: Same pressure each time, repeat each test, use a magnifying glass to check grooves, more testers between values.

questions.q: Diamond is ... on the Mohs scale.
Big question: how can we rank materials by hardness without a laboratory?
questions.a: A scratch test with testers of known hardness, then order the results.
